newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise amid very thin activity.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise amid very thin activity.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly higher Monday although there was virtually no trade on account of the closure of the U.S. markets for Veterans Day.
"Trade was sporadic, investors did not risk making trades without overseas references," said a trader.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 was flat at 83-3/4, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was marked $0.20 higher to 120.
Traders said the focus is likely to continue to be on the United States in coming days, with another batch of indicators due to be released from that country this week.
In addition, the Federal Open Market Committee of the U.S. Federal Reserve meets on Wednesday to decide on the course of interest rates.

On Tuesday some of the focus will go to the monthly Argentine treasury bill auction however. The Economy Ministry is due to auction 250 million pesos of 91-day bills and $250 million of 182-day bills.

But analysts maintained their optimistic outlook for the market. "Fundamentals remain unchanged and in that sense we maintain our positive short-term outlook," said analysts at Banco Rio in an investor note.
